sources.title: What is Kosher? > Basic Ingredients: meat only from kosher species and slaughtered under supervision; birds include chicken and turkey; dairy is milk and its derivatives; pareve covers eggs from a kosher bird, plants and fish with fins and removable scales; shellfish and all mixtures of meat and dairy are not kosher. Facts only, no text copied.
sources.licence: Copyright Kosher Australia Pty Ltd (Terms of Use, read 2026-10-28: no reproduction without permission). Only the facts are used; no text is copied.

sources.title: What is Kosher? > Mixtures: meat and milk (or derivatives) may not be mixed or cooked together; meat and fish may not be mixed. Facts only.
sources.licence: Copyright Kosher Australia Pty Ltd; facts only, no text copied

sources.title: What is Kosher? > Preparation: grape-derived drinks and cheese must be prepared by or under supervision of Jews/Rabbinic supervision (cheese, wine and grape juice stay unknown here). Facts only.
sources.licence: Copyright Kosher Australia Pty Ltd; facts only, no text copied

sources.title: Halal: pork is the most common example of haram food; blood and intoxicants such as alcoholic beverages are not halal; the majority of Islamic scholars consider shellfish and other seafood halal (schools of thought differ); vegetarian cuisine is halal if it does not contain alcohol. Secondary: it is a general reference, not the Halal Certification Authority.
sources.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (facts only, no text copied)

sources.title: Vegetarianism: the practice of abstaining from the consumption of meat (red meat, poultry, seafood, freshwater fish, insects and the flesh of any other animal); may also exclude by-products of slaughter. Secondary: Vegetarian Victoria and Vegetarian Society pages could not be read.
sources.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (facts only, no text copied)

sources.title: Vegan Pledge, "Vegan diet": a diet that consists wholly of plant foods, with no products derived from animals.
sources.licence: Copyright Vegan Australia; terms not read; only the definition (a fact) is used, no text copied

sources.title: Gluten-free diet: gluten is found in wheat (all varieties, including spelt), rye, barley and oats (in some people); naturally gluten-free single-ingredient foods include fresh fruit and vegetables, raw unprocessed meat and poultry, eggs, nuts and seeds, legumes, natural and minimally processed dairy, fats and oils, and rice and other gluten-free grains.
sources.licence: Copyright Coeliac Australia; terms not read; facts only, no text copied

sources.title: Allergen labelling (Standard 1.2.3 and Schedule 9, in force 25 February 2024), Table 1 names: wheat, fish, crustacean, mollusc, egg, milk, lupin, peanut, soy, sesame, almond, Brazil nut, cashew, hazelnut, macadamia, pecan, pistachio, pine nut, walnut, barley, oats, rye (if gluten), sulphites (10 mg/kg or more). An ingredient not on the list has no declarable allergen from it.
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 Australia (FSANZ site licence)

sources.title: FAQ: halal means permissible; haram or non-halal means not permissible; Australian red meat is hand-slaughtered. It gives no list of ingredients, so no halal flag is taken from it. Read to try to source halal definitions.

foods.name: Red lentil dal
foods.recipeBasis: Author's own simple recipe: 60 g dried red lentils simmered with onion, tomato, garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin, finished with a little oil. Nutrition is computed from raw (dry) ingredient weights; cooking changes and added salt are not modelled.
foods.priceBasis: Sample estimate: typical Melbourne supermarket cost of the raw ingredients for one serve, rounded to 10c; not an observed price.

foods.priceBasis: Sample estimate: typical Melbourne supermarket cost of the raw ingredients for one serve, rounded to 10c; not an observed price.

foods.priceBasis: Sample estimate: typical Melbourne supermarket cost of the raw ingredients for one serve, rounded to 10c; not an observed price.

foods.name: Potato and cauliflower (aloo gobi)

foods.priceBasis: Sample estimate: typical Melbourne supermarket cost of the raw ingredients for one serve, rounded to 10c; not an observed price.
